title: perf(canary): enhanced auto-detection and rollout guards for performance canaries
author: Alex Nguyen
release_notes: Enhances performance-canary auto-detection and rollout guards: adaptive baseline detection, hysteresis on regressions, configurable thresholds by route/model, richer alerting in Console. No behavior-breaking API changes.
description: Motivation: current perf canaries rely on static thresholds which cause noisy alerts and occasional false-positive rollbacks during traffic/seasonal shifts. This PR implements an adaptive auto-detection algorithm and stronger rollout guards so canaries surface real regressions while avoiding unnecessary rollbacks, improving reliability of automated rollouts. What this changes: 1) Auto-detection: a rolling-baseline window (configurable, default 1h) is used per-route to compute expected latency/throughput distributions. We use a combination of median+MAD and a two-sample KS test for distributional shifts to detect meaningful changes rather than simple percent differences. 2) Hysteresis & sustained detection: regressions must exceed threshold and persist for a configurable minimum-duration (default 5m) before triggering a guard action; transient spikes are ignored. 3) Multi-metric guards: checks now consider P95 latency increase, median latency shift, and throughput drop jointly. A weighted scoring function determines guard tripping to reduce sensitivity to single-metric noise. 4) Rollout actions: when a guard trips the rollout enters a paused state and can optionally auto-rollback if auto-rollback is enabled for the rollout. We added a safe fallback path that routes traffic to the previous stable model variant and emits a traceable rollback event. 5) Config/API: new canary config fields (baseline_window_minutes, sustained_duration_seconds, scoring_weights, enable_auto_rollback) with defaults that match current behavior for existing customers. 6) Observability: Console dashboard updates, new perf-canary logs and tracing hooks, and alert templates for on-call. 7) Testing: end-to-end tests that simulate sustained and transient regressions, unit tests for the scoring function and KS-based detector, and a small load test harness. Backwards compatibility: the default values preserve prior rollout behavior; feature gated behind a runtime flag `perf_canary_autodetect_v2` and rollout-level opt-in. Files changed (high-level): services/perf-canary/detector.py - new autodetect logic and tests; services/perf-canary/scoring.py - weighted scoring and hysteresis; services/perf-canary/config_schema.yaml - new config fields and validation; redwood-console/src/components/PerfCanaryConfigForm.tsx - UI controls for the new fields; redwood-console/dashboards/perf-canary.json - dashboard panels; infra/k8s/perf-canary-configmap.yaml - defaults; tests/perf_canary/e2e/test_sustained_regression.py - harness; docs/operations/perf-canaries.md - doc updates and runbook additions. CI: added unit tests and a small load suite; one flaky integration test (test_canary_rollout_flaky) failed on first run and was retried in CI and passed on rerun. Impact: reduces false-positive rollouts, improves signal-to-noise for SREs, and enables safer automatic rollbacks when configured. Rollout plan: feature gated rollout to 10% of accounts for two weeks, then enable as default if no major incidents are observed.

Suggested initial thresholds: sustained_duration_seconds=300, baseline_window_minutes=60, scoring_weights={p95:0.6, throughput:0.3, median:0.1}.
